title: Nebraska Sports: Cornhusker Pride
description: Cornhusker pride—stadium lore, dynasties, and football culture.

questions.question: Nebraska's football team once played as the Bugeaters—what nickname do they go by today?
questions.explanation: Lincoln sportswriter Cy Sherman tired of "Bugeaters" and borrowed a name sometimes pinned on Iowa. The 1900 team was first to wear it; the state adopted it in 1945.

questions.question: On Cornhuskers game days, which Lincoln venue becomes, by crowd size, Nebraska's "third-largest city"?
questions.explanation: Dedicated in 1923 to Nebraskans who served in the nation's wars. In 2023 a volleyball match drew 92,003 there, a record crowd for a women's sporting event.

questions.question: Since 1962, Memorial Stadium has held an NCAA-record streak of consecutive what?
questions.explanation: It began Nov. 3, 1962, with 36,501 fans for Missouri. No. 400 came in 2024—an overtime loss to Illinois—and the streak is still more than double any other school's.

questions.question: During Memorial Stadium's consecutive sellouts, who coached Nebraska to three national titles in the 1990s?
questions.explanation: Titles in '94, '95 and '97 (shared with Michigan). Fans still debate the 1984 Orange Bowl: down 31-30 to Miami, he went for two instead of a likely title-winning tie—and missed.

questions.question: Osborne's dominant 1990s offensive line earned what nickname?
questions.explanation: Line coach Milt Tenopir lost four starters after 1994, and the 1995 Pipeline still paved the way for 399.8 rushing yards a game. The Blackshirts? That's the defense.
